blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff; §§10/12.3 mixed-fat-object applicability
blocking.problem: The proposal changes launch-estimate and certificate invocation contracts without stating how a mixed fat object uses them. INDEX's general assertion that no north-star capability is removed does not supply the module boundary, launch-shim responsibility or certificate inventory required by the standing mixed-fat-object check. This is an omission in the proposed repair, not a request to redesign the accepted launch ABI.
blocking.fix: Add this paragraph to the recommended normative diff for §§10/12.3: “In a mixed fat object, native host code remains native. The host launch shim loads the selected marked ISA module and negotiates the token-alias binding feature with its runtime and scheduler. Execution derives token_aliases from the actual live handles supplied to that device invocation; tuple-based estimate and scheduling requests supply the partition explicitly. Alias-bearing schedules and certificate invocation records bind the selected module's object/closure identities and resolved device invocation, rather than treating the native host binary as one ISA object. Native entry points, argv/envp and unaffected host libc require no device token-alias entries; the alias-binding inventory covers the marked device closures and their invocations.”

suggestions: §10.1, legacy ABI paragraph: state “Absent an explicitly defined uniform-result certificate form, a legacy estimate request with token arguments and no alias binding returns E_ARG; the alias-aware function supports every consistent partition.” Alternatively define a certificate form quantified over all consistent partitions now. I would use the E_ARG default for the legacy entry point and retain exact coverage through the new entry point.

§15 and Conformance vectors: add a concrete Q witness. Use a memoryless oracle with body “lift.retval x” and an action containing “oracle_call @identity a (x) t f () (); oracle_call @identity b (x) t f () ()”. With a distinct primary token and all tuples equal, [0,1,1] must give a sole K65 carrier at the second call; [0,1,2] must give none. Both contexts remain valid. For the published CC witness, both args arrays hash to bf8eae8d885943f1948223391b24a677ec8eaefc4d39544bd6ed106277a211ed.
path_to_accept: Add B1's mixed-fat-object applicability paragraph to the proposed normative diff. No other blocking change is required.
summary: The identity gap is real and the partition repair is sound. The cited clause numbers, fixture pin and catalog/hash premises check out, including INDEX's conditional publication caveat. Revise only for the mandatory mixed-fat-object applicability statement.
